note: Generals are made the ones concluding an alliance 'with the Thurians ... with the Athenians'; source has the Thurians to be persuaded to ally with the Athenians.
replacement: After the Sicel disaster the Syracusans put off any immediate attack on the Athenians. Demosthenes and Eurymedon, whose forces from Corcyra and the mainland were now ready, crossed the Ionian Gulf with their whole armament to the Iapygian promontory. From there they started and touched at the Choerades Isles, off Iapygia, where they took on board a hundred and fifty Iapygian darters of the Messapian tribe. They renewed an old friendship with Artas the chief, who had supplied them with the darters, and arrived at Metapontium in Italy. Here they persuaded their allies the Metapontines to send three hundred darters and two galleys with them, and with this reinforcement they coasted on to Thurii. There they found that the party hostile to Athens had recently been expelled by a revolution, and so they stayed to muster and review the whole army, to see if any had been left behind, and to prevail on the Thurians to join their expedition wholeheartedly and, in the circumstances in which they found themselves, to conclude a defensive and offensive alliance with the Athenians.
